comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
SCOPE — started as "resolve bugs 1803 and jira-reb-1582" and grew, at operator direction, into: the structural link rule, the rebar doctor verb, a doctor-epic merge, and two follow-on defects the work exposed.

WHAT LANDED (12 merged changes)

Story affe-2b42-4ee4-4e12 (closed), two children:
- 7ab3-9df0-7a90-4ffd — blocking-link comparability is STRUCTURAL, not type-tier. Nearest common ancestor with a virtual-root sentinel (so parentless tickets are siblings and there is no undefined disjoint case). _TYPE_TIER and its three helpers deleted; _get_ancestors uncapped + cycle-guarded; is_redundant recomputed from the RESOLVED pair, inside the resolver, so add_dependency / the dry-run preview / the standalone resolve path all inherit the ancestor refusal. Merged 693a6bf41.
- 9ad7-d5a2-a664-4827 — the audit/repair check, shipped as `rebar doctor` (six changes: 1028, 1039, 1040, 1045, 1047, 1052).

Follow-ons the work exposed, both closed:
- fec5-d8bb-86cd-453e — link escalation was silent for library/MCP callers. Record now returns through five layers. Merged 1059 / 6f787da0529e.
- 6e4f-cad1-aa39-446a — retyping a ticket replayed a verdict computed under different criteria. Merged 1058 / eea930a64e20.

Superseded bugs 1803 + jira-reb-1582 closed duplicate. Doctor epics merged: dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6 canonical, 18ae-4f54-a85b-4ddb closed duplicates.

STORE REMEDIATION — 18 legacy bad edges found on this tracker, 12 repaired, 8 residual and provably inert (every endpoint closed, so none can reach ready/next-batch). Pre-repair anchor tag at 962624641cae.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
KEY DESIGN DECISIONS (and who made them)

1. Fold 1803 into jira-reb-1582 rather than fix separately — 1803 was a symptom of the type-tier policy, not an independent defect. Operator choice.
2. Escalate cousins per the 1582 spec. Two leaves in different sub-trees now escalate to their parents where they previously linked directly. Operator choice, taken knowingly: it inverted three existing tests while eight held unchanged, which was the main evidence the formulation was right.
3. A standalone `link-audit` verb REJECTED for core — rebar already had three detect-and-remediate surfaces (fsck --repair, validate --fix, this) with two different "fix it" flag names. Became `rebar doctor`s first check, framed as a named check list so later checks slot in without new verbs. Operator direction.
4. Fail OPEN on the retype fix rather than invalidate every attestation. Operator direction, and correct: adding ticket_type to the material fingerprint would have invalidated every certified ticket AND broken two hardcoded fingerprint SHAs at tests/unit/test_plan_review.py:1023-1024. The sidecar already recorded ticket_type, so the fail-open compare needed no schema change.
5. Do NOT remove quiet=True to fix the MCP silence. rebar-mcp speaks MCP-over-stdio; an unsuppressed print inside a tool call would inject a bare JSON object into the JSON-RPC stream. The defect was that stdout was the ONLY channel, not that it is suppressed — so the record became a return value.

EVIDENCE THAT MATTERED
- The retype defect is consequential, not theoretical: on scratch ticket cf19-d1e0-e817-4510 the SAME plan BLOCKs as a task and PASSes as a bug, because bug is exempt from criteria task is not.
- The store DRIFTS on its own: after remediating to zero scheduling-affecting findings, two NEW mis-escalated edges with OPEN endpoints appeared within hours. Re-parenting silently invalidates previously-correct links because comparability is structural.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
MISTAKES I MADE — recorded because the pattern repeats and the next agent should expect it.

1. TESTS THAT PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON — three times.
   a. Claimed twice that experiment had REFUTED a reviewer finding that run_repair self-deadlocks. Both probes ran against the synthetic graph-test tracker, which is NOT a git repo, so stage_and_commit bails before it ever takes the write lock and rev-parse HEAD returns empty. Every assertion compared "" to "". Against a REAL git-backed tracker: repair_finding without the outer lock = repaired in 0.1s; run_repair holding it = unrepairable after 60.0s on a flock timeout. The reviewer was right; I was wrong twice and had over-weighted my own null result against the live evidence (zero progress in 10 minutes was always more consistent with blocking than with slow pushes).
   b. The pre-repair tag test was tautological twice over: HEAD never moved between runs, and `git rev-parse` of an ABSENT ref echoes the ref name to stdout rather than returning empty, so the "tag must not exist" check passed on a non-empty string.
   c. On fec5, an earlier test draft stubbed rebar.link wholesale, so a mutation that swallowed the value in _python_leaf PASSED when it should have failed — through the exact layer the review had flagged.
   LESSON: a mutation check is only as good as the fixture. Verify the probe can detect the OPPOSITE before trusting a null result.

2. FILED A P1 BUG ON A MISREAD (480e, closed not_a_bug). Grepped for an import line, saw that same import fail in a bare interpreter, concluded the reconciler in-flight probe could never read the lock — without reading the four lines ABOVE it that insert engine_dir() into sys.path. The guard was correct; a reconciler pass really was in flight. /rebar-debug then proved it properly: 12 samples of a frozen heartbeat, then check_pass_lock returning False once the lease expired.

3. ASSERTED A PROPERTY THE SYSTEM DID NOT HAVE. Wrote in the story that the redirect record is "kept as the loud signal". True only on the CLI path; rebar.link() discards it. Became ticket fec5.

4. PRESENTED A CACHED RESULT AS A FRESH ONE. Reported that fec5 "passed cleanly under stricter task scoring" — it had not run at all (runner: reused). Operator caught it. The forced re-run returned BLOCK with 3 findings, including that the planned fix would have been a NO-OP because three layers dropped the return value. Became ticket 6e4f. USE --force when a re-review must actually re-run.

5. Destroyed my own composer.py edits with a `git checkout` during mutation cleanup; caught by a grep guard before commit.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
GATE OBSERVATIONS — what caught what, useful for calibrating trust.

- The COMPLETION VERIFIER (close gate) was the highest-yield gate by a distance. It caught SEVEN acceptance criteria I had written describing behaviour I shipped but never pinned: the pre-repair tag, init_only, --repair --dry-run, the reconciler in-flight refusal, the unrepairable path, the no-flags event count, and the non-blocking --repair invariance. Plan review and code review both passed every one of those gaps. Ticket 9ad7 took seven changes, five of them pure test coverage as a result.
- PLAN REVIEW was most valuable when the plan asserted something about code I had not read. It caught: _link_dry_run never inspecting the resolver error key; an is_redundant vs error-key contradiction I had introduced; that widening is_redundant would break the direct-parent test since a parent IS an ancestor; docs/event-schema.md carrying the tier rule; the help/overview/schema contract triangle; and — after --force — three unnamed drop points in the fec5 return chain.
- The CLOSE GATE correctly refused a plan edited after its review (stale-material) and a story whose child material had drifted (stale-pin-drift). Both were right.
- A close was once blocked not by an unmet criterion but by a CONTEXT BOUND: the ticket had grown to 29,267 chars against a 24,000 limit. Resolved by condensing the description to 8,132 while preserving all 17 criteria verbatim, NOT by --force-close.

ENVIRONMENT NOTES FOR THE NEXT AGENT
- The tracker is a SYMLINK shared by every worktree on this host (~56). Several background sessions write it concurrently; expect write-lock contention and "push-retry merge skipped" warnings.
- `git push gerrit` can fail with "remote unpack failed: Missing tree". Retry with `git push --no-thin`. This checkout is a partial clone and it recurs.
- docs/cli-reference.md is GENERATED (scripts/gen_cli_reference.py) with a CI drift gate. Hand-written prose there is discarded; conceptual docs belong in docs/ticket-model.md.
- Advertising --output in help text is contract-enforced TWICE: a schema in schemas.OUTPUT_SCHEMAS (keys are underscored) AND a driver in CLI_OUTPUT_DRIVERS that runs the command live and validates real output.
- test_help_overview_coverage enforces THREE directions, incl. routable-set == pinned-help-set; an `if sub ==` dispatcher arm must be added to that tests own individual set.
- monkeypatch.undo() reverts EVERY patch made through the fixture, including conftests git isolation. Restore by re-patching with a saved original instead.
- Gerrit rebases on submit WITHOUT re-running CI. Two changes green in isolation can be red combined (this happened: 228b x 7e77, ticket 2c38). When stacking on an unmerged change, restack onto its CURRENT patchset and verify the combination locally.

OPEN — one deliberate loose thread: re-parent/unparent invalidating the dependency graph. Recorded as in-scope on epic dabb-7d4b-f5bc-40e6 (auto-remediate when unambiguous, or DENY with a clear error), with the drift evidence above. It has NO ticket of its own yet. doctor is the backstop, not the primary defence.
